proof_chain.name: RankerRealCurvature.eq_zero_of_squaredEuclideanNorm_eq_zero
proof_chain.method: Each coordinate square is bounded by the nonnegative finite square sum. A zero sum forces every coordinate square, and then every coordinate, to vanish.

proof_chain.name: RankerRealCurvature.realCoordinateGradient_eq_zero_of_global_minimum
proof_chain.method: Let g be the actual coordinate gradient at z. A true global minimum makes t↦F(z+t*g) locally minimal at 0. Fermat applied to the already established actual scalar derivative gives dot(g,g)=0; the coordinate square sum is therefore zero and g=0.
proof_chain.premises: Only the true global-minimum property. Neither n>0 nor mu>0 is needed for this stationarity conclusion because the directional derivatives were already proved for every finite n,m and mu.

proof_chain.name: RankerRealCurvature.realObjective_quadratic_growth_at_minimum
proof_chain.method: Use realObjective_lower_between from z to w. Substitute the derived zero gradient and rearrange.
proof_chain.premises: n>0 and the true global-minimum property. Positive mu is needed when growth is later used to control displacement, but the displayed inequality itself holds for every mu.

proof_chain.name: RankerRealCurvature.realObjective_minimizer_unique
proof_chain.method: Two global minima have equal objective values. Quadratic growth from z1 to z2, positive mu and square-sum nonnegativity force zero displacement. Coordinate equality gives z1=z2.
proof_chain.premises: n>0, mu>0, and the genuine global-minimum properties of both comparison points.

proof_chain.name: RankerRealCurvature.originalReal_gradient_eq_zero_of_global_minimum
proof_chain.method: Specialize stationarity to the already joined original exact-real coordinate data.

proof_chain.name: RankerRealCurvature.originalReal_quadratic_growth_at_minimum

proof_chain.name: RankerRealCurvature.originalReal_exists_unique_global_minimizer
proof_chain.method: Obtain the actual minimizer from the independently qualified originalReal_exists_global_minimizer, then use the derived original uniqueness theorem. Unique existence is a conclusion, not a premise.
